correctness.rationale: A chosen vertex of T(n) is an edge of K_n. Maximum induced degree at most one is equivalent to vertex-disjoint P3, K2 and unused vertices; the exact integer constraints (3a+2b+c=n and 2a+b=floor(2n/3)) force all three residue patterns. At n=3k no one-edge exchange can change a P3 vertex block, and center changes form Cartesian products of K3. At n=3k+1 an unused vertex can swap into any path position, yielding all block partitions, and each two-pair optimum has a direct adjacent singleton optimum. At n=3k+2 a concrete two-move pair/triple exchange implements arbitrary label transpositions through the unique pair. Enumeration and degree formulas are exact block/local counts. The two included programs independently check all small orders 3..9 from direct definition and block enumeration, respectively; no infinite conclusion depends on those computations.

originality.rationale: The novelty claim is confined to connectivity and exact components of the maximum-dissociation one-vertex exchange graph of T(n). The 2011 full-text Orlovich et al. paper supplies the scalar optimum for all line graphs of Hamilton-path graphs and the underlying P3/K2 reduction, and is properly credited; neither theorem implies that fixed triple partitions are invariant at n divisible by three nor constructs reconfiguration paths with singleton/pair buffers. residual_risks: A differently indexed, unpublished or inaccessible account of one-exchange P3-packing reconfiguration could cover the claim; searching is not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: This is a sharp infinite modular connectivity phenomenon in optimal-solution reconfiguration, not simply the already known dissociation number. At multiples of three, an exact triple-block invariant creates n!/(6^k k!) components K3^square k; in the other two residue classes a singleton or edge acts as a buffer enabling reachability of every optimum. This structural discontinuity and component isomorphism classification are natural information unavailable from the maximum-cardinality scalar; no general downstream theorem is asserted.
